sources.title: Jean README
sources.locator: Overview, setup, features and component boundaries
sources.finding: Tauri/React workspace runs installed coding CLIs with existing subscriptions in worktrees and multiple sessions. Git/PR/review tools, local summaries, web access and Linux server routes are described.

sources.title: Jean license
sources.locator: Root license grant
sources.finding: The cited root license governs this repository distribution, subject to component notices.

sources.title: Jean Web Access and Headless
sources.locator: Defaults; Headless server; Install; Updates
sources.finding: Full browser UI uses host HTTP/WebSocket; Linux server has installer/systemd route. Desktop defaults off, localhost and token-required.

sources.title: Jean local-first and security
sources.locator: What Jean stores; Providers; Safe defaults
sources.finding: Projects, messages, archive state and preferences stay on the host; selected coding providers receive their own requests.

sources.title: Jean GitHub, Linear and reviews
sources.locator: Context; Mr Robot; Review workflows
sources.finding: GitHub/Linear/Sentry intake, beta issue sweeps and integrated PR investigation, feedback and merge are documented.

sources.title: Jean desktop Cargo manifest
sources.locator: Tauri dependency and application package
sources.finding: The desktop uses Tauri 2; the UI is React per the project technical overview.

sources.title: Jean v1.0.14
sources.locator: Release notes
sources.finding: v1.0.14 adds remote token-authenticated MCP, linked delegated sub-sessions/result return, review sessions, screenshot galleries and HttpOnly Web Access sign-in cookies. Experimental Agents closes to new users.

sources.title: Jean architecture guide
sources.locator: Chat-to-chat delegation (Jean MCP)
sources.finding: Describes chat-to-chat delegation through the Jean MCP and notes manual MCP clients. It does not tie Jean MCP to the v1.0.14 remote endpoints.

sources.title: Jean backends, models and MCP
sources.locator: MCP
sources.finding: Jean discovers MCP servers from the backends installed on the host.

sources.title: Jean FAQ; Local and remote
sources.locator: FAQ; Local and remote
sources.finding: Jean explicitly states it is free forever with no paid tiers, feature gates or usage limits. Users supply coding-agent subscriptions/API access and their own machines. Remote jean-server agents continue after the controlling laptop closes. Desktop Windows/Linux builds work but need more testing.

sources.title: Jean Archive vs delete; Retention and restore; Recovery; Quit confirmation
sources.locator: Archive vs delete; Retention and restore; Recovery; Quit confirmation
sources.finding: Sessions/worktrees can be archived or permanently deleted; archive retention days are configurable and archived work can be restored. Finished unread sessions have a popover. The app documents crash-state persistence/emergency recovery and confirms quitting while runs execute.

sources.title: Jean Context; Commit and sync; Pull request work
sources.locator: Context; Commit and sync; Pull request work
sources.finding: Save/Load Context persists summarized snapshots; Review stores revisitable findings in the Review panel. Magic commands include commit/push, PR creation/update, review, conflict resolution and confirmation before reverting the last local commit. Templates, model/backend/provider and effort defaults can be edited.

sources.title: Jean docs/developer/architecture-guide.md
sources.locator: MCP; backend integration; Background Tasks
sources.finding: Architecture guide documents Jean MCP project/worktree/session tools, usage/model controls and commit/PR/review wrappers. Saved secrets are owner-scoped files with optional 24-hour cleanup, not encrypted; all agents share an OS user. GitHub issue polling retries failed starts at most three times and defers rate-limited projects 15 minutes. Native resume/session IDs are persisted for several backends, and run logs retain output for Claude, Kimi and Antigravity.

sources.title: Jean v1.0.14 platform release assets
sources.locator: Assets: Windows x64 setup/MSI; Linux AppImage/deb/rpm; platform testing note on jean.build
sources.finding: Release assets include Jean_1.0.14_x64-setup.exe, Jean_1.0.14_x64_en-US.msi, Linux amd64/arm64 AppImage/deb and aarch64/x86_64 RPM. Homepage says Windows/Linux builds work but need more testing. No installation was run.

sources.title: Jean Antigravity support at v1.0.14
sources.locator: README.md lines 40-48, v1.0.14, commit af882efe7ac2e19c3f462a983137a171d58fd994
sources.finding: Jean v1.0.14 lists Antigravity among its runnable AI backends and explicitly labels the integration beta.

sources.title: Jean runnable backend enum
sources.locator: Backend enum and Deserialize implementation, lines 103-155
sources.finding: The closed backend enum supports Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, Pi, Command Code, Grok, Kimi, Devin, Antigravity and Muse. Gemini maps to Antigravity rather than Gemini CLI; Aider is absent.

sources.title: Jean Web Access authentication
sources.locator: http_server/auth.rs, session.rs and server.rs; inspected preferences and API dispatch for role or SSO models
sources.finding: Web Access authenticates against one instance token and session cookies. The scoped application has no human membership, named role or enterprise SAML/OIDC SSO implementation. Sharing the instance token does not establish separate human identities.

sources.title: Jean persistent worktree and tracker data
sources.locator: Worktree/ProjectsData schemas; project storage and GitHub/Linear issue integrations; chat Session schema
sources.finding: The native persisted entities are projects, worktrees and chat sessions. Worktrees store labels and external GitHub/Linear identifiers, but no independent product-owned issue lifecycle/catalog is implemented. Repository issue records remain in external trackers.

sources.title: Jean server Docker distribution
sources.locator: Docker notes, lines 309-337
sources.finding: Jean publishes a server Docker image that runs jean-server and its coding CLIs inside one container with a persistent /home/jean volume. This is whole-server container deployment, not a separate security sandbox per session.

sources.title: Jean process and workspace isolation
sources.locator: chat host/process launchers, project worktree commands and server deployment configuration; searched VM, microVM, Docker
sources.finding: The local runtime runs installed coding CLIs as host processes and separates working files using Git worktrees. It implements no VM isolation allocator. A manually provisioned VM used as the server host is external infrastructure.

sources.title: Jean telemetry control inspection
sources.locator: jean-core preference schema, HTTP dispatch, frontend settings and dependency manifests; searched telemetry, analytics, opt-out and DO_NOT_TRACK
sources.finding: The inspected application has no product telemetry opt-out setting or control. No application analytics collector was found; Sentry integration retrieves the user project issues rather than reporting Jean analytics. Provider controls remain separate.

sources.title: Jean custom Claude provider credentials
sources.locator: Custom CLI provider profile handling and known authentication environment keys
sources.finding: Jean supports configured Claude CLI provider profiles with user-provided ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN for model access. This model-provider charge is separate from free Jean software.

sources.title: Jean Devin execution location
sources.locator: DevinLocation enum and Devin backend launch configuration
sources.finding: The Devin backend offers Local and Cloud execution locations. Cloud here is the external Devin/Cognition service, not Jean-operated managed compute.
